version_note: 2010 Nueva versión (album: El tiempo por testigo... A Sevilla) — opener / user's entry ear; version-specific NetEase ID points to the 2010 cut.
focus_relevance_note: Opener — 2010 Nueva versión with 28-voice Polígono Sur children's choir. The user's entry into Dorantes (red-heart 2025-11-10). Sets up the dual-version frame: this re-translation is the inner mirror of every translation edge in the map.

Family root — Lebrijano (Dorantes' uncle, Peña-Perrate-Pinini-Bacán dynasty) opens cante hondo to long-form poetic-narrative material on Persecución. The methodological precedent for Dorantes' later piano-led re-orchestrations of cante. Translation sense: cante hondo carrying conceptual album-form narrative.

Founding rupture — non-traditional instruments (drum kit, electric guitar, sitar, flute) become acceptable inside flamenco. Lorca text in Camarón's cante. Every translation aesthetic Orobroy descends from passes through this 1979 break.

Commercial canonization of modernized flamenco — congas, bongos, electric bass entering flamenco rumba for the first time. Paco's widened palette is the precondition Dorantes inherits and ports to solo piano a generation later.

Generational precedent — Amador brothers' 'blueslería' (pure blues at the rhythm of bulerías) is the immediate model for foreign harmonic vocabulary inhabiting flamenco's body without dissolving it. Eleven years before Orobroy puts jazz-piano voicings in the same body.

Methodological elder brother on the flamenco-piano axis — Chano (b. Cádiz 1960) debuts 1993, Dorantes (b. Lebrija 1969) debuts 1998. Same dual-influence pairing — Bill Evans + Paco de Lucía — both pianists publicly cite. El Puerto (from Piano Ibérico) keeps the solo-piano flamenco vocabulary audible.

Spanish-classical-piano root — Iberia processes cante-jondo melisma and Andalusian rhythmic cells through a piano-virtuoso harmonic language. Dorantes inverts the gesture (flamenco materials rendered in late-Romantic + jazz harmony). RomArchive Dorantes portrait paraphrases his own citation of Falla / Granados / Albéniz; held at consensus tier because the citation is paraphrased rather than verbatim.

Solo-piano source dialect — sustained left-hand ostinato over a singing right hand developing long-form melisma is the public template Spanish music press repeatedly compares Orobroy to. Jarrett (Jasmine in the user's red-heart, 2023-10) is the closest in-library bridge to the jazz-piano language Orobroy translates.

Lateral bridge — Buena Vista re-opens the Spanish-Cuban cultural axis Bebo Valdés had been part of pre-exile, making the next stop's Cigala × Bebo encounter culturally legible. Red-heart cluster (4 album tracks, 2023-08 → 2024-01) is the user's earliest documented bend toward Iberian-Latin translation.

Lateral counterpart to Orobroy's translation aesthetic — Cigala's flamenco voice in Bebo's Cuban piano body, vs Dorantes' jazz piano in flamenco's body. Same five-year window, same Javier Limón / Trueba ecology. Paradigmatic 'gene wears a different coat' — both languages stay audibly separable.

Exact-year contemporary peer — the 1998 Barcelona Jazz Festival improvisation that became Spain pairs flamenco guitar with Latin-jazz piano in the same year Orobroy is recorded. Two instruments split between two players doing what Dorantes' two hands do alone.

Lateral female-cante peer — Triana-born deep-soleá voice, family-circuit linkage to Lebrija (her mother Pepa Vargas and Dorantes' father are second cousins). Her 2001 debut Esperanza Fernández features Dorantes accompanying her on the canonical soleá. Translation here: cante hondo voice carrying contemporary recorded-album form.

version_note: 1998 original — solo piano with wordless cante melisma, from the album Orobroy. This is the canonical anchor row.
focus_relevance_note: Anchor — naked 1998 solo piano with wordless cante-jondo melisma over a Bill-Evans-like ostinato. 'Orobroy' is Caló (Iberian Romani) for 'good day'. After 12 prior stops the bare original becomes a perceptual recalibration: the listener can hear what the 2010 orchestration added and what it covered. Triple-coated translation — jazz piano voicings + bulería compás + cante jondo melisma + Caló title — all four layers still legible.

Female-voice translation downstream — Equatorial Guinean parents, Mallorcan upbringing, copla-flamenco-jazz triple-coding. Javier Limón's production places Buika in the same 2000s-Madrid translation circuit Lebrijano helped seed. Translation: copla and cante carrying jazz-diva phrasing, both languages audibly separable.

Cante-jondo voice of the same generational cohort — Linares records Lorca's Canciones Populares Antiguas (1931 collection) on Flamenco Vivo. Same poetic-recovery line Lebrijano (Persecución) and Dorantes (Orobroy as wordless cante) participate in. Red-heart hit (2026-02-10) — the user's deep-cante closure ear is already on this voice.

Gen Z deep-cante translation — Llergo (Pozoblanco; ESMUC under the same teacher as Rosalía) carries inherited cante from her grandfather Pepe in olive fields into contemporary production. Translation here: olive-field cante carrying ambient electronic dressing while staying audibly cante.

Gen Z mainstream articulation — ESMUC flamenco-studies thesis project (El Mal Querer, 2018) brings non-flamenco surface (pop-trap production, sampled palmas, drill hi-hats) into the centre of flamenco compás and cante phrasing while keeping both layers audibly separable. The clearest 2010s descendant of the M1 translation aesthetic Orobroy crystallised in 1998.

song: Tú Me Dejaste de Querer (feat. Niño de Elche, La Húngara)
focus_relevance_note: Mainstream pipeline downstream — El Madrileño extends the post-Rosalía permission for mainstream Iberian-pop with flamenco at the centre. Niño de Elche's bulería voice + La Húngara's gypsy-rumba phrasing on a contemporary urban arrangement: three traditions in one piece, all still audibly themselves. Edge held at consensus (was hypothesis in map; the citation chain through Rosalía is well-documented).

song: Romance de la monja (que no quiso serlo)
focus_relevance_note: Current-generation Sevillian-cante voice — Lagos (Jerez) extends Lebrijano's poetic-conceptual cante-with-contemporary-arrangement methodology into 2024. Red-heart hit (2026-05-04) — the user is currently inside this exact voice. Consensus tier: geographic and methodological proximity to the Lebrija cante line is documented; Lagos has not publicly cited Lebrijano as direct lineage so the connection sits below fact.

Family-circuit closer — same album as the 2010 Nueva versión at position 1 (El tiempo por testigo... A Sevilla). Dorantes returning to his uncle Lebrijano's voice on the same record where he re-translates his own Orobroy. Red-heart hit (2025-11-27) — the closure is already in the user's ear. The 12-year self-translation and the 34-year family voice meet on one disc; the episode loops back to this convergence.
